newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd Webber embroiled in UK election battle.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd Webber embroiled in UK election battle.

text.p: Opposition leader Tony Blair said on Tuesday he wanted to encourage millionaires like composer Andrew Lloyd Webber and urged the wealthy to stay in Britain if Labour won the imminent election.

"I want entrepreneurs to stay here and succeed. I want a culture of entrepreneurial success that rewards talent. I want more people to become millionaires through enterprise," Blair said at a breakfast for entrepreneurs in London.
But Prime Minister John Major's ruling Conservatives, reacting to reports that Lloyd Webber was considering moving abroad if Labour won, warned his example would be followed by many rich people.
"Mr Blair wants to tax them (millionaires) more," said Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine, unveiling a poster attacking Labour's tax policy.

Asked if Lloyd Webber's fears were justified, Heseltine added: "He's quite right... He's a man who has brought huge revenues and prestige to this country, and who is seriously thinking of leaving if Labour were to be elected.
"Of course there would be many more like him."

Blair, who has moved his party away from its socialist roots to the middle ground of politics, tried to soothe concern that Labour would revert to its old high-taxing ways and capitalism would once again become a dirty word.
"Too often British entrepreneurs take their ideas abroad because they are not given support," said Blair. Labour are strong favourites to win the election which must be held by May 22.
Old-guard Labour figures welcomed the prospect of Lloyd Webber, one of Britain's 20 richest people, quitting Britain. Lloyd Webber made a similar threat before the 1992 election.

A group of left-wing Labour members of parliament tabled a parliamentary motion, which will not be debated, praising the reported decision by Lloyd Webber, responsible for such musical successes as Evita and Cats.

They said the group "welcomes the undertaking given by multi-millionaire Sir Andrew Lloyd Webber that he will quit Britain should Labour win the general election, believes such a promise provides an extra incentive to vote Labour and looks forward to Sir Andrew keeping his promise." ($1=.6227 Pound)
